correctness.rationale: Writing \(s_i=\sqrt{V_i+\eta^{-2}}\) converts each boundary exactly to \(s_i\sqrt{\log(\eta^2/(a_i/s_i)^2)}\). For \(0<\alpha<e^{-1/2}\), every feasible \(a_i/s_i\) lies in the strict-convexity region of this scalar function, so weighted Jensen gives the unique common-ratio allocation \(a_i=\alpha s_i/S\) and the displayed minimum. The fixed-allocation coverage extension uses only a union bound. Expanding the equal-split logarithms around \(L_t=\log(\eta^2S(t)^2/\alpha^2)\) gives the stated KL coefficient. An independent numerical reconstruction reproduced the closed-form objective on a three-clock example.
risks: The convexity hypothesis is sufficient and is used exactly as stated; the audit does not extend the theorem to larger alpha.
The coverage statement is only for allocations fixed independently of the experiment, not post-hoc plug-in clocks.

value.rationale: The source setting has a concrete design choice—how to prespecify a familywise error budget across arm-level anytime-valid intervals when target variance clocks are imbalanced. The theorem solves that natural finite-clock optimization exactly, gives a simple square-root-rate prescription, quantifies the cost of equal splitting by a KL term, and states the validity boundary against data-dependent reallocation. This is more than a normalization check or arbitrary parameter slice.
risks: The practical gain depends on availability of credible deterministic target clocks; no adaptive allocation theorem is supplied.

limitations: Common mixture parameter \(\eta\), deterministic target clocks, and \(\alpha<e^{-1/2}\) only; no post-hoc random-clock allocation is validated.
